subject: Acme incident — logs preservation, export, and residency questions
messages:
From: Jason Smith <j.smith@acme-networks.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Forensic Lead <forensics@cyberfirm.io>
Date: 2026-02-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme incident — initial questions about logs

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Acme's security team is standing up a post-incident review and we need to understand what logs Redwood can preserve and export for our external forensic team. Specifically: 

- Which system/application logs are available (API request logs, model-serving request traces, KV/cache events, autoscaler events, audit logs)?
- Where those logs are stored (cloud region / S3 bucket / customer-controlled bucket)?
- Can Redwood provide raw log exports with timestamps and request IDs, and include any request payload metadata needed for correlation?
- Any residency constraints (we need the logs to remain in the US), and whether you have to redact content that could contain PII before export.

We anticipate needing an initial set of logs covering the 72-hour window around the incident and then a longer retention snapshot (up to 180 days) pending the investigation. Please confirm timing for a secure export and whether chain-of-custody manifests can be provided.

Appreciate a concrete preservation plan so we can coordinate with our external forensics partner (cc'd).

—Jason
Senior InfoSec, Acme Networks
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Smith <j.smith@acme-networks.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-16T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme incident — logs preservation, export, and residency questions

Jason — thanks for the specifics. Short answers up front, longer plan below.

- What we can preserve: API request/response logs (headers, timestamps, request IDs), service traces (latency spans), scheduler/autoscaler events, control-plane audit logs (who changed configs), and persisted storage access logs (S3 access logs, DB audit). We do not store long-term model internal KV cache contents by default; ephemeral KV cache metadata (eviction, size) is available in traces for the timeframe.
- Residency: production logs for Acme are in our us-east-1 account by default. We can stage exports to a customer-controlled bucket in us-east-1 for transfer.
- Redaction: we can provide raw logs but will apply redaction on PII upon explicit request or per legal instruction.
- Export formats: gzipped JSONL for structured logs; we can include an export manifest with hash checksums for chain-of-custody.

Proposed immediate steps (I can action with Security Ops):
1) Place a 14-day legal hold on the relevant log streams for the 72-hour window centered on the incident time.
2) Snapshot S3 buckets and capture access logs and object versions.
3) Export service traces and request logs as JSONL with request_id index.
4) Produce a chain-of-custody csv manifest (who exported, hashes, timestamps).
5) Deliver export via a pre-signed s3 URL to the Acme bucket or SFTP if you prefer.

Can you confirm: (a) target export destination (Acme S3 bucket in us-east-1 preferred), (b) whether you require redaction before export, and (c) if forensic consultant needs any additional indexed fields (user_id, session_id, or specific model invocation metadata)?

I will CC Rafael from CS and Evelyn from Security Ops once scope confirmed.

—Vivek
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jason Smith <j.smith@acme-networks.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Forensic Lead <forensics@cyberfirm.io>
Date: 2026-02-16T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme incident — logs preservation, export, and residency questions

Vivek — thanks. Confirming:

- Destination: Acme-managed bucket in us-east-1 (we'll share bucket ARN and a short-term write role).
- Redaction: please do NOT redact at source. We need raw logs for correlation; Acme legal will handle PII protection post-receipt.
- Fields: include request_id, timestamp (UTC), client_ip, api_key_id (partial masked if necessary), model_name, invocations payload hash, and any trace_id.
- Retention ask: initial preserve for the 72-hour window; then a hold for 180 days while investigation continues. We may reduce later but provisionally 180 days.

Forensic lead: can you confirm the preferred delivery mechanism?

—Jason
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Jason Smith <j.smith@acme-networks.com>
Date: 2026-02-17T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme incident — logs preservation, export, and residency questions

Team — per Jason's confirmation, I'm initiating the preservation/export workflow. Summary of actions I'm asking Security Ops to execute now: 

- Legal hold: 180-day hold on relevant log streams (72-hour incident window + 7 days buffer) — do not delete, rotate, or purge.
- Snapshots: create immutable snapshots of S3 buckets in us-east-1, and capture S3 access logs and object versions. Mark snapshots as write-once where supported.
- Trace/export: export API request logs, service traces, autoscaler events, and control-plane audit logs as gzipped JSONL. Include the following indexed fields: request_id, trace_id, timestamp_utc, client_ip, model_name, invocation_hash.
- KV/cache: include eviction and cache-miss metrics and the cache metadata manifest (not full in-memory KV content).
- Chain-of-custody: generate chain_of_custody_manifest.csv with exporter identity, export timestamps, SHA256 checksums, and target bucket path.
- Delivery: provision a short-lived write role to Acme's bucket in us-east-1; if they prefer, we can provide a pre-signed upload endpoint.

Attachments: forensic_export_checklist.pdf (checklist for exports), chain_of_custody_manifest.csv (template).

Please do NOT perform any irreversible deletion until counsel signs off. Rafael — Rafael, coordinate the IAM role and CS touchpoint with Acme's cloud team. Evelyn — own the snapshot and manifest generation. Monica — loop in Legal for formal hold and any GDPR-specific guidance on cross-border transfer.

On Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 10:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jason — thanks for the specifics. Short answers up front, longer plan below.
> ...

—Vivek
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Jason Smith <j.smith@acme-networks.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme incident — logs preservation, export, and residency questions

Vivek/Evelyn — quick legal note: Counsel requests we extend the hold to 180 days as a precaution and avoid any deletion or lifecycle transitions (to Glacier/Deep Archive) until the investigation and counsel review complete. If any logs subject to EU/EEA residency rules are identified, do not transfer cross-border without legal approval — for Acme this currently looks US-only, but confirm when exports are staged.

Also: please capture account consent records and any Data Processing Agreement references in the chain-of-custody manifest. I'll open a legal hold ticket and tag SEC-2143.

—Monica
General Counsel (acting), Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Smith <j.smith@acme-networks.com>, Forensic Lead <forensics@cyberfirm.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T13:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme incident — logs preservation, export, and residency questions

Jason / Forensics team — confirmation below and next steps: 

1) Preservation complete: Security Ops has applied a 180-day hold on the identified streams and created immutable snapshots of the corresponding S3 buckets in us-east-1.
2) Exports: We will export the 72-hour incident window as gzipped JSONL and place exports in your Acme bucket (please share bucket ARN and write role by EOD). Expected export artifact size estimate: 12–18 GB compressed.
3) Chain-of-custody: manifest.csv will be included and checksums verified.
4) Delivery ETA: export will be staged within 7 business days after we receive your write role. If you need expedited turnaround, indicate priority and we will escalate.

Attached: forensic_export_checklist.pdf; chain_of_custody_manifest.csv (template).

If you confirm the bucket details I will trigger the upload and notify you when the pre-signed path is live.

Thanks — Vivek
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
